stories.h: King tides and storm surge flood Washington's outer coast
stories.s: Major flood stage at Westport, flooded streets in Ocean Shores and a Highway 101 closure near Raymond hit the coast. Forecasters warned significant flooding could continue into Thanksgiving; stay off jetties and seawalls.

stories.h: Skokomish River heads toward near-record flood in Mason County
stories.s: Heavy Olympic rain pushed the river past flood stage, threatening homes, farmland, Skokomish Valley Road and Highway 106. It may dip Friday but could rise again over the weekend. Never drive into floodwater.

stories.h: Coastal floods, but Seattle-area reservoirs are running low
stories.s: Even as king tides swamp shorelines, Seattle's Cedar and Tolt watersheds have had about half their normal rain since October, forcing an emergency pump. Most of the state is abnormally dry or in drought.

stories.h: Longview senator drafts mill tank safety law after 11 deaths
stories.s: Sen. Jeff Wilson plans a bill letting Labor and Industries inspect and certify chemical tanks at pulp mills, with daily fines up to $5,000, following May's deadly Nippon Dynawave tank rupture.

talking.h: Darnold practices fully as Seahawks eye 49ers
talking.s: Sam Darnold, nursing rib and quad injuries, was a full participant Wednesday. Coach Mike Macdonald hasn't formally named him the starter but calls him the go-to quarterback when healthy. Official designations come Friday.

talking.h: Huskies take on No. 13 Oregon in rivalry finale
talking.s: Washington, 7-4 and just outside the polls, visits 8-3 Oregon at Autzen Stadium Saturday night in a prime-time NBC game.

talking.h: Cougars close a 2-9 season on Senior Day
talking.s: Washington State hosts San Diego State in Pullman Saturday, honoring 12 seniors in its season finale after a loss at Texas State.

coming.h: Coastal flood warning for Grays Harbor coast
coming.s: NWS expects 3 to 4 feet of inundation 10 a.m.-6 p.m. today, with numerous road closures likely; a watch follows Friday. Puget Sound lowlands are under a warning until 10 a.m.

coming.h: Winter storm warning for North Cascades
coming.s: Another 6 to 12 inches of snow and gusts to 40 mph in the Whatcom and Skagit Cascades until 4 a.m. Friday; travel may be very difficult to impossible. Carry chains.

coming.h: Ferries run holiday schedules; tides limit some sailings
coming.s: Several routes run modified or holiday timetables today. Port Townsend/Coupeville drops an evening round trip through Friday, and Vashon routes restrict long or low vehicles through Sunday.
Senior Day kickoff at 3:30 p.m. at Gesa Field in Pullman, on The CW.
Kickoff 4:30 p.m. PT at Autzen Stadium on NBC.
Seattle returns from its bye to face San Francisco, with Darnold's status set to be finalized Friday.
